classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate each expression before and after distributive expansion, checking that both routes agree.

content.prompt: First, substitute $x=5$ in each expression and evaluate it. Next, expand the brackets and again substitute $x=5$.

answer.worked:
Substitute first:
$$\begin{align*}2(5+3)&=2\times8\\2(5+3)&=16\end{align*}$$
Expand:
$$\begin{align*}2(x+3)&=2\times x+2\times3\\2(x+3)&=2x+6\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the expanded expression:
$$\begin{align*}2\times5+6&=10+6\\2\times5+6&=16\end{align*}$$

Substitute first:
$$\begin{align*}5(2\times5+4)&=5(10+4)\\5(2\times5+4)&=5\times14\\5(2\times5+4)&=70\end{align*}$$
Expand:
$$\begin{align*}5(2x+4)&=5\times2x+5\times4\\5(2x+4)&=10x+20\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the expanded expression:
$$\begin{align*}10\times5+20&=50+20\\10\times5+20&=70\end{align*}$$

Substitute first:
$$\begin{align*}2(5-2)&=2\times3\\2(5-2)&=6\end{align*}$$
Expand:
$$\begin{align*}2(x-2)&=2\times x-2\times2\\2(x-2)&=2x-4\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the expanded expression:
$$\begin{align*}2\times5-4&=10-4\\2\times5-4&=6\end{align*}$$

Substitute first:
$$\begin{align*}6(5-3)&=6\times2\\6(5-3)&=12\end{align*}$$
Expand:
$$\begin{align*}6(x-3)&=6\times x-6\times3\\6(x-3)&=6x-18\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the expanded expression:
$$\begin{align*}6\times5-18&=30-18\\6\times5-18&=12\end{align*}$$
